texts.title: A garden that needs less water

paragraphs.text: Hotter summers and bans on using hosepipes have led many gardeners to rethink the way they grow plants. A garden that needs less water can still be attractive, but it requires some planning.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Choosing the right plants is the most important decision. Plants from dry regions, such as lavender and rosemary, have small or silver leaves that lose little moisture and can survive weeks without rain once established.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The soil itself can hold more water if it is improved. Adding compost helps sandy soil to keep moisture, and a thick layer of bark or gravel on the surface reduces evaporation.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: When watering is necessary, timing makes a difference. Watering early in the morning or in the evening means less water is lost to the sun, and a thorough soak once a week encourages deeper roots than a light daily sprinkle.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Many gardeners also collect rainwater. A simple container connected to a roof gutter can store hundreds of litres over the winter, providing a free supply for the driest months.
paragraphs.label: E
